label: real accepting reply, Opus 5.5, round 1, JSONL line 1
reply: **No.** EntryPoint v0.7 also charges a 10% penalty on unused execution gas (callGasLimit plus paymasterPostOpGasLimit): each 5,000,000-limit operation that uses only about 150,000 gas costs the paymaster an extra ~485,000 gas, which is over four times the actual cost and goes to the bundler's beneficiary address, so the bundler profits by draining the deposit.

label: real rejecting reply, GLM 5.3, round 1, JSONL line 3
reply:
**Yes.**

The EntryPoint pre-charges the paymaster for the full `callGasLimit`, but after execution it measures the gas actually consumed and refunds the unused portion (plus a fixed `postOp` overhead), so inflating `callGasLimit` to 5,000,000 on a ~150,000-gas operation does not increase what the paymaster ultimately pays — the real griefing risk here is instead that the paymaster signs *any* op, so a malicious user could submit an operation whose execution genuinely burns up to 5M gas (or reverts mid-execution, forcing the paymaster to cover the consumed gas plus `postOp` costs), but that is a function of gas actually used, not of the declared `callGasLimit`.

label: solution
reply: No. EntryPoint v0.7 also charges the paymaster a 10% penalty on unused execution and postOp gas limits.
